part: live spike (local Docker), ADR-0001 protocol, option A
commit_note: Tested stand and scripts are in the same commit as this report (spikes/m4-live/). SHA is reported in the commit/PR, a commit cannot contain its own SHA.
author: Claude Code (local executor, M4 live part)

environment.contextforge_version: v1.1.1 (GitHub release 2026-11-10, latest non-prerelease on 2026-11-20); digest is the linux/arm64 image

contextforge_config_under_test.IDENTITY_CLAIMS_SECRET: random 32 bytes in .env, separate from JWT_SECRET_KEY

environment.topology: 2 teams (t-alpha, t-beta) x 2 agents (users with team-scoped API tokens, expires 1 day). Per team: gateway echo-direct-<team> (tool not renamed), gateway echo-alias-<team> (tool renamed via custom_name = alias), virtual server vs-<team> with both tools. All visibility=team.

advisories.latest_patched_floor: GHSA-w8vq-gj3v-h664 (medium, < v1.0.8, patched v1.0.8); all other GHSA patched at <= v1.0.7
advisories.release_notes_security_items_v1.1.1: token exchange delegation, CEL tool validation, webhook HMAC replay protection (PSIRT ADV0369535, opt-in, webhook plugin only - not identity propagation)

mechanism_observed.source_file: /app/mcpgateway/utils/identity_propagation.py in the pinned image (sha256 of file 5482d2d4..., identical to git tag v1.1.1)
mechanism_observed.signed_payload: f"{user_id}:{email}" only. NOT signed: teams, admin, roles, method, path, body, time, nonce, audience.
mechanism_observed.meta_mode: _meta.user = {id, email, full_name, teams, is_admin, auth_method}; carries NO claims_signature (docs say it should; code does not add it)
mechanism_observed.secret: IDENTITY_CLAIMS_SECRET, falls back to JWT_SECRET_KEY when unset (config.py: 'uses JWT_SECRET_KEY if unset'); symmetric, shared by every upstream that verifies
mechanism_observed.principal_value: user email (mutable attribute). The token's immutable sub (UUID) is not propagated.
mechanism_observed.team_header_missing: documented X-Forwarded-User-Team-Id is not sent; only the teams list
mechanism_observed.signature_stability: identical signature for every request of the same user (R-fresh-vs-old-signature.signature_identical_to_captured = true)
mechanism_observed.service_auth_contextforge_to_upstream: none: echo receives no Authorization header from ContextForge (gateway auth_type not set); upstream can only tell ContextForge from others by network
mechanism_observed.agent_jwt: HS256, iss=mcpgateway, aud=mcpgateway-api, sub=user UUID, teams=[<team uuid>], token_use=api, jti, exp present (decoded locally, signature not shown)

criteria.text: Agent cannot influence tenant_id and principal via arguments, headers or _meta
criteria.scope: calls that go through ContextForge (/rpc and virtual server)
evidence: F-headers-rpc, F-headers-vs: agent sent X-Forwarded-User-Id/Email/Teams/Team-Id/Admin/Claims-Signature of t-beta-a1; echo received only ContextForge values for t-alpha-a1 (teams=t-alpha uuid, admin=false, real signature); forged Team-Id/Admin absent
F-meta-rpc, F-meta-vs: agent sent _meta.user of t-beta-a1 with is_admin=true; echo received _meta.user replaced by ContextForge (t-alpha-a1, is_admin=false)
F-args-rpc, F-args-vs: tenant_id/agent_id/principal in arguments reach the upstream unchanged as data; identity headers/_meta stay t-alpha-a1
criteria.caveat: Holds only with default passthrough_headers. Not tested: gateway passthrough_headers containing X-Forwarded-User-*. Tenant (teams) is not covered by the signature, so this protection ends at ContextForge (see criterion 2).

criteria.text: A request that bypasses ContextForge does not get an identity
evidence: B-direct-noid: direct POST to echo without identity -> verifier rejects (no identity headers) - OK
B-direct-forged: direct POST with forged headers and zero signature -> verifier rejects (bad signature) - OK
B-direct-teamswap: direct POST with captured t-alpha-a1 headers and x-forwarded-user-teams swapped to t-beta uuid -> verifier ACCEPTS principal t-alpha-a1, tenant t-beta (team is not signed)
R-replay-direct-66s: direct POST with captured headers -> verifier ACCEPTS

No service authentication from ContextForge to upstream: echo log shows no Authorization header on any ContextForge call (peer 172.22.0.4) vs attacker calls (peer 172.22.0.1) - only network position differs
criteria.reason: Any party that sees one request (log, proxy, compromised neighbour upstream sharing the HMAC secret) gets a permanent bearer identity, and can choose its tenant.

criteria.text: Replay of intercepted identity after > 60 s is rejected
evidence: R-replay-direct-66s: headers captured from P-direct-rpc-t-alpha-a1, replayed 66.0 s later directly to echo -> accepted by the verifier
R-fresh-vs-old-signature: a legitimate call 66 s later carries a byte-identical signature
signed payload has no iat/exp/jti/nonce/aud (identity_propagation.py build_identity_headers)
criteria.reason: Replay protection cannot be built on the connector side: nothing time- or request-bound is signed.

criteria.text: Identity works on all paths: direct tools, virtual servers, aliases
evidence: 16/16 delivered with correct principal and team for 4 agents x {direct tool via /rpc, alias via /rpc, virtual server + plain tool, virtual server + aliased tool}: P-direct-rpc-*, P-alias-rpc-*, P-vs-direct-*, P-vs-alias-*
headers and _meta identical in shape on all four paths; tools/list and initialize to the upstream also carry identity headers
criteria.caveat: Global /mcp streamable endpoint: tools/call with a team-scoped API token -> 'Access denied' (RBAC tools.execute without server scope; streamablehttp_transport.py:2213), never reaches upstream - identity there not observed (P-direct-mcp-*). Alias replaces the tool name: the original name is not callable (P-alias-origname: Tool not found). direct_proxy gateway mode and resources/prompts paths not tested.

criteria.reason: Only v1.1.1 was run; no live upgrade from an older pinned version. MC-05 belongs to stage C.
criteria.static_evidence: identity_propagation.py at v1.0.11 and v1.1.0 is byte-identical (sha256 e7f7aa54...); v1.1.1 only adds a per-gateway config parameter; the signed payload f"{user_id}:{email}" is unchanged across these versions.

tenant_isolation_informational: X-rpc-beta-tool, X-rpc-beta-alias: t-alpha-a1 calls t-beta tools by name via /rpc -> 'Tool not found', not delivered
X-vs-beta: t-alpha-a1 to t-beta virtual server -> HTTP 403; ContextForge log: 'Server ... is team-scoped to <beta>, token is scoped to teams [<alpha>]'
X-vs-mismatch: t-beta tool via t-alpha virtual server -> not delivered
tools/list via /rpc: each agent sees only its team's tools (checked during setup debugging, not in results.json)

verify_items_for_cloud_executor.SEC-02: JWT has a 'teams' claim (list of team uuids) and aud=mcpgateway-api; tokens are HS256 with JWT_SECRET_KEY
verify_items_for_cloud_executor.SEC-03: Propagation and signing are both off by default (config.py defaults false). Signed claims: user_id:email only, HMAC-SHA256, no iss/aud/iat/exp/jti/tenant.
verify_items_for_cloud_executor.TEN-01: team-scoped visibility of tools and virtual servers confirmed on /rpc and /servers/{id}/mcp (above)
verify_items_for_cloud_executor.GR-example principal: ContextForge propagates the email as id; an immutable id would have to be the JWT sub (UUID), which is not propagated

preliminary_decision.option_A: NO-GO: fails criteria 2 and 3; tenant not signed; symmetric secret (falls back to JWT_SECRET_KEY); principal is a mutable email.
preliminary_decision.next: Option C (own adapter: plugin or sidecar issuing Ed25519 JWS with aud, exp 60 s, jti, body hash) per ADR preference. Not tested live here: whether a ContextForge plugin hook on v1.1.1 sees UserContext on every path and can add a header to the upstream request.
preliminary_decision.overall_M4: conditional - GO only after option C is proven on the same stand; otherwise roadmap NO-GO alternative

not_run_or_not_checked: option C and option B prototypes
direct_proxy gateway mode, resources/read, prompts/get paths
global /mcp path for tools/call (blocked by RBAC for team-scoped API tokens)
multi-worker / Redis setup, session pooling identity isolation
